name: Keys on Try Three
why_it_works: Buyers who were turned down feel alone and ashamed. A story with two failures before the yes gives them permission to try again, and puts the professional in the role of the guide who kept going. Counting the tries makes progress visible.

hook.pattern: Slide one names the number of rejections before the keys, as a count.
examples: Try one. Try two. Try three: keys.

variables.name: buyer_label
variables.description: How the buyers are described, anonymized or with consent
variables.example: A nurse and a first-time dad

variables.name: try_one
variables.description: What happened on the first try
variables.example: outbid by $22,000 on a house they loved

variables.name: try_two
variables.description: What happened on the second try
variables.example: the loan fell through a week before closing

variables.name: what_changed
variables.description: The concrete thing that changed before try three, a full sentence starting with a capital letter, no end punctuation
variables.example: We rebuilt the offer around a later move-in date the seller needed

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What viewers can do next, starting with a capital letter
variables.example: Book a free 20-minute buyer plan call

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, from compliance/packs.json, shown as small on-screen text
variables.example: Equal Housing Opportunity. Brokerage and license # shown.

slides.headline: Two no's. Then keys.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 close-up of a hand holding a new house key on a simple keyring, blurred front door behind, soft morning light

slides.headline: Try one
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 photo of a for-sale sign with a sold rider in front of a modest house, overcast sky, muted colors

slides.headline: Try two
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 photo of a kitchen table with paperwork and a closed laptop, evening light, two coffee mugs, quiet

slides.headline: What changed
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 photo of an agent's hands pointing at a printed plan on a table, warm office light, no buyer faces

slides.headline: Try three
slides.visual_prompt: Client-supplied photo of the real buyers at their new door, with written consent; for a composite story, an empty open front door in golden light, no people

slides.headline: On try one or two?
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 branded card in {{brand}} colors with the offer and license number in clear type

craft.technique: Rule of three with a counted structure
craft.notes: Label each attempt as 'Try one', 'Try two' so the swipe has rhythm. Keep the failures specific and short. The 'what changed' slide is the professional's real value, shown as a decision, not a boast. The win slide is one word.

do_not: Promise approval or a winning bid
Shame the buyers for the failed tries
Show the buyers' faces or address without written consent
compliance: Real estate: include brokerage name and license number on the final slide as your state requires; follow fair housing rules, no language about who belongs in a neighborhood
Mortgage: no promise of approval or specific rates; include NMLS ID and Equal Housing Lender/Opportunity logo where required
Financial and insurance: no guarantee of outcomes or savings
Composite or anonymized stories must say so on the first or last slide
Real buyers appear only in client-supplied photos with written consent; never generate faces to stand in for them
